subject: POC Plan & workload intake for Acme Corp

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (POC)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the call today — really appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call recap:
- Goal: Run a 4-week POC to validate Redwood Inference for Acme's customer support summarization pipeline and evaluate latency/cost at production load.
- Primary success criteria (from your side): 1) >95% fidelity on extractive summary tests (per your eval suite), 2) 95th percentile latency < 350ms for 1–2k token requests, 3) cost-per-1k tokens <= $X (TBD after workload intake).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Ben to send a draft POC plan (success criteria, timeline, owners) and a short workload intake table for your engineers to fill in (RPS, token lengths, concurrency, burst patterns).
2) Camila to scope technical on-call / SRE involvement and proposed initial infra config.
3) Sophie to share a representative sample of 100 requests (anonymized) or a sample workload CSV.

Attachments: poc-outline.pdf (draft plan).

Target timeline:
- POC kickoff: week of Mar 8
- 4-week evaluation window: Mar 9 – Apr 5

Please let me know if the criteria above map to what you expect. If yes, I'll ship a detailed plan with owners and the workload intake table for your team to complete.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Nguyen <sophie.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (POC) — Draft POC plan and workload intake

Sophie — thanks for the questions. Below is a concise POC plan and the workload intake we discussed. I've kept the items high-level so we can align quickly; Camila and Laura are on copy for technical and CS ownership.

POC Plan (4 weeks) — high level
- Objective: Validate Redwood Inference for Acme support summarization at production traffic and cost targets.
- Success criteria (finalized with you):
  * Accuracy: >=95% pass rate on your human pass/fail eval for the 100-sample set (we will run automated ROUGE and your human labels).
  * Latency: 95th percentile response time < 350ms for typical 1–2k token requests during steady-state.
  * Stability: 99.9% uptime for API for test traffic and graceful degradation on spikes.
  * Cost: unit cost aligned with committed budget (we will provide a cost estimate after workload intake).

Evaluation plan & ownership:
- Week 0 (prep): redwood provides POC infra + test harness; Acme provides anonymized sample workload and eval criteria. (Owners: Ben/Laura: Redwood; Sophie/Engineering: Acme)
- Week 1 (ingest & baseline): deploy model variant, run baseline tests, measure latency/cost. (Owners: Camila + Acme Eng)
- Week 2–3 (stress & tuning): run sustained load tests, iterate on batching/quantization, measure 95/99 percentiles. (Owners: Camila, Acme Eng)
- Week 4 (final evaluation & handoff): run final eval suite, review metrics, decide next steps (Dedicated / Hosted). (Owners: Ben, Laura, Sophie)

Timeline:
- Mar 8: Kickoff and infra provisioning
- Mar 9–Mar 15: Baseline tests and validation
- Mar 16–Mar 29: Stress testing and tuning
- Mar 30–Apr 5: Final evaluation and review

Workload intake (please fill or confirm):
- Primary endpoint / use-case: customer-support summarization API
- Typical requests per second (steady-state): 8 RPS
- Peak sustained RPS (during business hours): 40 RPS
- Burst peaks (short spikes lasting <5s): up to 180 RPS observed during ticket surges
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + expected completion): 1,250 tokens
- 95th percentile token length: 2,000 tokens
- Max tokens you may send for some cases: 4,096 tokens
- Concurrency (simultaneous open requests): ~60 concurrent requests during peak
- Expected monthly token volume (estimate): ~350M tokens
- Required latency SLO: p95 < 350ms, p99 < 800ms

If any of the numbers above are off, please correct them. Based on these numbers Camila recommends starting the POC on a 2-node dedicated pool with model variant: open-model-XL-8bit (or hosted equivalent) with batching tuned to 128ms window and KV cache settings enabled. This should hit your latency/cost targets for the 4-week window; we'll iterate after baseline results.

Attachments: sample-workload.csv (CSV with example rows), poc-outline.pdf (detailed plan).

Next steps (short):
1) Sophie: share anonymized sample workload CSV and confirm RPS/peak numbers by EOD Tue 3/3 if possible.
2) Procurement: if you want, loop procurement now — we'll share a short SOW and trial terms.
3) Redwood: Camila to provision test cluster and share API keys (scoped to POC) on kickoff.

Let me know and I'll send calendar invites for kickoff.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Nguyen <sophie.nguyen@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC Plan — technical notes and recommended config

Hi Sophie — quick technical notes from the SE side based on Ben's intake table: 

1) Model & infra recommendation (initial):
   - Model variant: open-model-XL-8bit (quantized) — balance latency and cost.
   - Pool size: 2x A100-equivalent nodes (dedicated pool) for the POC; we can scale by 1 node if baseline falls short.
   - Batching: start with target batch window 100–128ms; max batch size tuned to keep p95 under 350ms.
   - Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for repeated context (customer threads) to reduce token compute.

2) Observability we will provide:
   - Token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, per-node GPU utilization, and trace IDs for problematic requests.

3) Requirements from Acme to provision test cluster:
   - Anonymized workload (sample-workload.csv) or direct API access to a sandbox endpoint (preferred).
   - Test dataset credentials (if any private S3 buckets) or a way to pull 100 sample payloads.

Security note: by default the POC will use Redwood-hosted test cluster (hosted in US region). If you require VPC/private deployment for the POC we can spin up a private test plane but that will add ~3 business days to provisioning.

I'll provision a test cluster once we receive the sample CSV and confirm kickoff date.

Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
